text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.7% today, closing at $154.03, as oil prices surged on geopolitical risk. News that Qatari mediators were holding talks aimed at restarting U.S.-Iran negotiations spooked markets—the risk of renewed American-led attacks on Iran, a major oil producer, sent both U.S. crude (up to $103.37/barrel) and world oil prices (at $123.10) sharply higher. For a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost profitability on the barrels they pump out of the ground.

The move also reflects a broader momentum: the stock is up 5.13% over two weeks amid tightening global fuel supplies and escalating Middle East tensions. Tankers are still moving crude through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian attacks, but the freight premiums they command signal real supply risk, keeping crude prices elevated and supporting oil majors' earnings outlook.
